newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Eicher Motors 96/97 net sales up.
newsitem.headline: India's Eicher Motors 96/97 net sales up.

text.p: India's Eicher Motors Ltd said on Thursday that its net sales for financial year 1996/97 (April-March) had risen 25 percent to 3.25 billion rupees.
Its sister firm Eicher Tractors Ltd, posted a 23 percent rise in 1996/97 net sales to 3.90 billion rupees, the firm said in a statement. It did not give comparative figures.
The statement said the Eicher Group's turnover increased by 23 percent to 9.19 billion rupees as compared to 7.47 billion in the previous year.

The Eicher Group's flagship company, Eicher Limited, formed of Eicher Tractors, motorcycle manufacturer Royal Enfield and gear-maker Ramon and Demm, recorded total sales of over 5.55 billion rupees, showing a growth of 20 percent over the last fiscal year, the statement said.
The group's net profit was estimated at 470 million rupees, an increase of 15 percent over the corresponding period last year, it said.
The statement said Eicher Limited sold 23,130 tractors and 22,680 bullet motorcycles in 1996/97.
Royal Enfield's plans to enhance the capacity to 45,000 motorcycles were on target with the completion of the first phase which boosted existing capacity to 30,000 from 24,000.
The second phase was expected to be completed in the next fiscal year, the statement said.
It said plans were underway to double the capacity of the Ramon and Demm plant to 500 tonnes per month from the current level of 250 tonnes a day.
